title: 8 Funniest ‘Far Side’ Comics About Fruits and Vegetables
summary: Gary Larson’s comic strip The Far Side featured jokes about all kinds of things, including fruits and vegetables. Here are the 8 funniest.
content: Decades after Gary Larson concluded his comic strip The Far Side back in 1995, fans of the series continue to read it regularly, and new fans are discovering it all the time. Some of Larson’s most beloved comic strips feature animals drawn in his signature style, including dogs, chickens, and especially cows . He often gave these animals human-like intelligence and other anthropomorphic traits and depicted them in very human-like scenarios.

title: Magic: The Gathering’s Most Notorious Vampire Almost Broke Commander
summary: How Edgar Markov created Innistrad’s vampire bloodlines and became one of Magic: The Gathering’s most popular Commanders.
content: Most Commanders in Magic: The Gathering have to show up on the battlefield before they can do anything. But Edgar Markov can make you the most dangerous player at the table while he’s still sitting in the Command Zone. Cast a one-mana vampire on your first turn, and Edgar gives you a second vampire for free. Do it twice on turn two, and you have six creatures before some players have cast their first spell.

title: HBO Officially Teases New Thriller Series from Dark Creators
summary: The creators of Dark return to produce an HBO mystery thriller series based on a German children's book, Der Struwwelpeter.
content: The 2017 German sci-fi mystery thriller series Dark aired for three seasons on Netflix, gaining critical acclaim and a global cult following. Its complex plot explored the paradoxical nature of time travel through strange mysteries in the fictional town of Winden, Germany.

title: 35 Years Later, Hollywood’s Deadliest Feud Is Still Its Most Reliable Fantasy Formula
summary: The vampire-werewolf rivalry didn’t begin with the ancient feud many people assume. So why is Hollywood so fascinated by it?
content: At the time, the interaction, while hilarious, also made perfect sense. Popular culture was deep in the thrall of Stephenie Meyer’s Twilight , which famously pits a vampire and a werewolf against each other for the affections of a human girl. But a decade later, the idea that vampires and werewolves would be natural enemies seems a bit odd.
